lines.note: Iiqijen means before eating; Xocujen is the preferred form and xocuno maye spells out that relation. The scan prints Meliù with a grave and without final s; keep that anomaly and its following comma.
Antes de comer is the complete Portuguese explanation of the preceding Japanese forms. This indented continuation ends with a visible period.
Iiqimot denotes food or something to eat, matching cuimono and Couſa de comer. Restore initial I from the upright type; the final t represents the historical checked ending and is not expanded.

Iiqin is explained as teaching letters or their reading, iiuo voxiyuru. The Portuguese specifies reading without their meaning in the next row; enlargement shows an abbreviation mark above the final e, giving ſẽ rather than unmarked ſe.
The sense of the letters is what the preceding ſẽ excludes. Retain o ſentido dellas and do not add a word or punctuation at the line boundary.
Iiqirô names a food container, explained by putting food inside. The scan has upright Ii and a circumflex on ô; bocetas belongs to the historical Portuguese description of boxes.

runs.text: caixas altas, & bem ornadas em que metem

lines.note: These are tall and well-decorated boxes in which something is placed, continuing the Iiqirô definition. Preserve ornadas and the final unpunctuated metem.
The boxes contain things to eat. This short row completes the definition and is not a separate entry; the entire phrase and final period are visible.
Iiqiǔ is personal rest, expressed by mizzucara yaſumu. The final marked u is worn but its caron is visible; the Portuguese ends in pro without a printed hyphen.
Pria completes propria from the preceding row: rest of one’s own person. Preserve the two distinct long-s types in peſſoa rather than replacing them with a ligature or modern s.
Iiquan is an official rank, with tçugui tçucaſadoru suggesting a subordinate or next-ranking office. The gloss begins Certo grao de; both Japanese cedillas remain visible.
Dignidade completes the description of a grade of office or rank. The short continuation and its final period are fully contained in the line crop.

This separate entry names a large monastery or temple complex. Enlargement gives the final character the pointed, non-descending form of v, so the anomalous bǒv is selected instead of the draft bǒy; do not normalize its spelling from the expected vocabulary. The supplied NINJAL checkpoint independently lists bǒv, supporting this choice without overriding the scan.

runs.text: com muitas caſas, ou ermidas em circuito.

lines.note: The monastery has many houses or hermitages around it. The phrase em circuito completes the architectural description, not the preceding entry about official rank.

runs.text: Deſde antão pera cà, ou desde aquelle tẽ-

lines.note: Iirai means since then up to now. Preserve antão, cà, the second desde, and the visibly hyphenated abbreviated tẽ-; the text continues in po below.
Completes tẽpo atègora, the interval extending to the present. The scan has a grave in atègora and an upright S marking written usage; neither is silently modernized.

Iireǒ is glossed as monastery revenue. Restore the initial I and preserve the printed eǒ sequence and Tera tçucaſadoru, even though the Japanese paraphrase is not a literal equivalent of revenue; do not replace it with an expected landholding term. The supplied headword index also preserves Iireǒ, so its eǒ is not emended to iǒ.
Iiriqi denotes one’s own strength, mizzucaraga chicara. The first-person gloss begins Minhas, ou and continues below; the scan confirms the Japanese possessive ga.
Proprias forças completes the definition. The example Iiriqide taſucaru co- begins the statement that salvation or rescue cannot be obtained by one’s own power; its final co- continues below.

runs.text: Não ſe pode ſaluar hum por ſuas

lines.note: Tonaranu completes the negative Japanese construction. The Portuguese reads ſaluar, to save, not faluar; the native scan also supports the word separations pode ſaluar and por ſuas rather than the OCR’s merged strings.
The sentence concludes that a person cannot be saved by their own powers. Preserve the repeated forças proprias, which belongs to the example’s explanation rather than an omitted headword.

runs.text: Ter mão em ſeu parecer. Vt,

lines.note: Iiriǔ concerns maintaining or insisting on one’s own opinion. The example repeats the headword at the right edge, with the caron-marked u visible and no inferred terminal hyphen.

The continuation tano cocorouo yameyo calls for abandoning the attitude described; the Portuguese begins a prohibition on following one’s own opinion. Preserve the explicit voſ- division into the next row.

runs.text: ſo parecer com des fazer no dos outros.

lines.note: Completes voſſo and warns against disparaging others’ opinions while insisting on one’s own. Retain the provisional printed spacing des fazer and the wording no dos outros rather than rewriting the sentence.

Iiſacu is one’s own making or workmanship, mizzucara tçucuru. The apparent italic H in the draft is the damaged upright Ii initial; restore the complete roman headword while preserving the nasal abbreviation hũ.
The work is done by one’s own hand. Cono ſaqeua jiſacugia says that this sake is one’s own production; the Japanese example is upright after the italic Vt apparatus.

runs.text: Eſte vinho he feito de minha mão, &c.

lines.note: The Portuguese renders the example as wine made by my own hand. Preserve Eſte and the printed ampersand-c abbreviation rather than modernizing the historical type or wording.
Iiſacuno yaſai refers to vegetables one has grown oneself. The gloss begins Ortaliça plantada por and continues in the following row; the paragraph sign is present.
Completes planting with one’s own hands, then introduces Coreuo jiſacuni itaita, making this oneself. Preserve the printed mãos and the attached particle sequence Coreuo.

Itaita completes the past-tense example, translated as doing this with my own hand. The historical verb form is not regularized to a modern Japanese ending; retain the provisional Iſto ligature expansion.

runs.text: Iiſan. Mizzucara fomuru. i, Vagamiuo fo-

lines.note: Iiſan is self-praise. Mizzucara fomuru and Vagamiuo fomuru give two Japanese paraphrases, separated by the upright i,; the second verb is visibly divided fo- / muru.
Muru completes fomuru. The Portuguese means praising oneself; its final word is meſmo with m, not the OCR’s meſino, as confirmed by the complete italic letterforms.
Iiſô denotes the religious members of a monastery or temple. Restore the damaged upright Ii initial from the scan instead of the provisional r; the final vowel carries a circumflex.
Iiſon is glossed as a child, with chigo and mago supplied as Japanese equivalents. Preserve the comma between those forms and the historical Portuguese Minino.
Iiſot denotes soldiers. The headword’s middle types are faint, but the retained long-s and checked final t agree with the visible sequence; the brief gloss is complete.
Iiſsǒ here means true form, matching macotono catachi and Verdadeira figura. Preserve the visibly mixed long-s plus short-s pair and the caron over ǒ.

The next, separately aligned Iiſsǒ concerns true reports or news, not the preceding sense of form. Restore its missing initial I and retain the short s in the synonym sǒ rather than harmonizing it with the headword.

Iit is the sun or day, equated with fi; Iit, guet pairs sun and moon. The initial letter in both occurrences is upright I, not F or long-s. Keep guet unaccented because the small mark above it is not a secure printed vowel accent.
This separate Iit means truth, macoto, rather than sun. Iitni is the adverbial expression, translated beginning De ver; the scan has no terminal hyphen after ver.

Dade completes verdade. The next example is Iitna coto, a true thing: enlargement supports n in the adjective ending na, not the draft’s u, and the Portuguese explicitly confirms the attributive meaning.
Iita combines oneself and other people, explicitly paraphrased as mizzucara, tanin and Eu, & outros. This is a new headword; retain the comma between the Japanese components.
Iitatomoni yorocobu says that oneself and the others rejoice together. Todos juntamente begins the matching Portuguese statement, continued below.
Nos alegramos completes the first-person plural translation, we all rejoice together. Its short physical row and final period are retained.
Iitai here is declining or reluctance, not the substance sense below. Restore the initial I; the gloss repugnancia is retained despite locally weak type, and the example continues with voyobanu.

Iitaini voyobanu means there is no need to decline. The Portuguese likewise says there is no reason to refuse. Separate second-pass enlargement establishes the grave over a in hà; preserve it along with the historical voyobanu and recuſar spellings.

This distinct Iitai is one’s own substance or body, mizzucarano tai. The scan supports b in ſubſtancia rather than the OCR’s ule sequence; the internal st ligature expansion remains provisional, without a broader normalization of this type.
Iitan is one’s own sorrow or lamenting, mizzucara naguequ. The Portuguese begins Propria with P, not F; retain the printed tristeza and the complete final row above the rule.

Iitbo is sunset or dusk, explained by fino cure and figure. The scan supports t, not r, in the headword and shows it flush left; preserve the space before the alternative marker l and the historical figure spelling.
Iitboni nozomu concerns the sun reaching sunset. The Portuguese states that the sun sets; its final S is an upright written-register label, separate from the italic explanation.
Iitbot likewise denotes sunset, with fi votçuru, the sun falling. Retain final t and the cedilla, and give the visibly upright closing S its own roman type.
Iitden is true transmission or tradition, matching macotono tçutaye. The Portuguese begins Tradição, ou and continues with an alternative formulation below.
True doctrine completes the definition of Iitden. The final S is upright and indicates written usage; it is not part of the italic noun phrase.
Iitdǒ is the way of truth, macotono michi. Correct the initial F-like OCR reading to I and Macorono to Macotono from the native type. The final verda has no printed hyphen.
De completes verdade, followed by the equivalent true doctrine. This is the continuation of the preceding way-of-truth entry, with no new headword.
Ii teqi means one’s own enemy, explicitly mizzucarano teqi and Meu inimigo. Restore the initial I but retain the scan’s separation Ii teqi instead of silently joining the compound.
This Iitgo means at midday. Restore the initial I, retain the historical meo spelling, and separate the upright written-usage S from the italic Portuguese gloss.
A separate Iitgo means a true word or statement, rather than noon. The native headword is Iitgo, correcting the draft ticgo; preserve the singular Portuguese Palaura.
Iitgon means true words, as macotono cotoba and Palauras verdadeiras confirm. Restore the upright Iit sequence in place of Fie, while keeping the explicit terminal ver-.
Dadeiras completes verdadeiras, the gloss of Iitgon. This is the whole short continuation; its final period is visible and not shared with the next headword.
Iitguet pairs the sun and moon, fi and tçuqi. The Portuguese reads lũa with a nasal mark, not lia. The example begins with wholly upright Iit at the right edge and has no printed hyphen.
Together with Iit above, guet xeino ſanquǒ names the three lights: sun, moon and stars. The scan supports e in guet and a word space before xeino, correcting guotxeino; retain the caron on final ǒ.
The three lights are explicitly listed as Sol, lũa, & eſtrellas. Preserve the tilde and the inherited long-s/st reading rather than altering the astronomical explanation.
Iitgui is a true matter, glossed by macotono gui and Couſa verdadeira. The scan clearly gives tgui, including a descending g, not the provisional squi sequence.
Iitmiǒ is a true or proper name, macotono na. Preserve the final caron and the printed pro- division of the Portuguese word completed below.

runs.text: prio nome com que ſe hum aſina, &c.

lines.note: Prio completes proprio; the explanation specifies the real name used when signing. Retain the historical single-s aſina and the ampersand-c abbreviation.

runs.text: Febre rija que dà em homem de forte

lines.note: Iitnet is defined in the dictionary’s historical medical vocabulary as a strong fever in a person of robust constitution. The damaged word after que reads dà, not di; the small accent is selected as grave from the native impression.

Compreiſão completes the description of constitution. Qionet is then contrasted as a fever occurring in people of weak constitution; preserve this historical word rather than substituting modern Portuguese terminology.
Completes the contrast with people of frail constitution. This is still the explanation of Qionet on the preceding row and makes no present-day medical claim.
Iitǒ is answering oneself, vareto cotayuru. The scan separates Reſponderſe from aſi and reads meſ-, not moſ-, before the line division; the full phrase is completed by mo below.
Mo completes meſmo. Iimon jitǒ is the self-questioning, self-answering example, followed by an explicit reference to Iimon; the reference is upright after italic Vide.

runs.text: Penetrar per ſi, & cair nas couſas,

lines.note: Iitocu means grasping or coming to understand something for oneself. Preserve per ſi and cair nas couſas in the historical Portuguese explanation rather than replacing them with a modern paraphrase.
The continuation closes the self-understanding gloss with &c., followed by Bup., the upright Buddhist-usage label. The label’s final period belongs with its roman letters, not a separate italic run.

The headword reads Iit ro, true way, followed by macotono michi. Enlargement confirms the space and an unmarked final o, not the garbled hibro. The Portuguese reads caminho with a, correcting cominho. The NINJAL entry likewise records Iit ro as two written units.
Iittai is true substance, macotono tai. Restore the initial I instead of F and retain the double t; the existing internal st ligature expansion in ſubſtancia is left provisional.

runs.text: Adu. Modo de apertar, ou fechar al-

lines.note: Iitto is labelled as an adverb and describes closing or squeezing something tightly. Adu. and the explanation are italic; the visibly divided al- begins algũa across the row boundary.
Gũa completes algũa in the explanation of grasping something in the hand. Teni jitto ni- begins the Japanese example of gripping firmly; preserve the explicit ni- division.

runs.text: Ter fechado na mão algũa couſa com

lines.note: Guiru completes niguiru, to grip, from ni- on the preceding row. The Portuguese explains holding something tightly in the hand; retain algũa with its tilde on u and the final com leading into força below.

Força completes the firm-grasp explanation. The next example repeats Iitto before ximuru, tightening firmly; a faint second t survives between the clearer first t and o, so it is restored rather than keeping Iito.
Efficacia completes the explanation of tightening effectively or forcefully. The scan includes i after ff; restore that letter instead of the draft’s effcacia, without adding an accent.
Iittocu is explained by touono tocu, ten benefits or virtues, matching Dez proueitos. Preserve the printed double t and the older numeral touo rather than modernizing the Japanese.

runs.text: ¶ Item, Hũa certa laya de Dôbucus, de que

lines.note: A second sense is a particular kind of Dôbucus garment. The scan has a pointed circumflex over o, not the draft’s tilde; contrast it with the plainly nasal Hũa on the same row. The garment name is Japanese embedded in the Portuguese explanation.
The garments are used by shaven secular people, completing the second Iittocu sense. Preserve vſão and the distinction between secular wearers and monks implied by the printed wording.
Iit yei is the sun’s image or ray, fino cague. Restore the initial I in place of the long-s OCR error, but retain the printed space within the headword.

The example Iityei mizzuni xizzumeri describes the sun’s image in the water. The headword is joined in this example, unlike the preceding entry label; preserve that spacing difference and the lone unhyphenated article A at the edge.
The Portuguese explains that the sun’s likeness appears in the water. This is visibly indented as a continuation; preserve nagoa as printed instead of separating or modernizing it.

runs.text: Certa dignidade no moeſteiro dos Iẽxùs.

lines.note: This Iixa is a monastic rank in the community named Iẽxùs in the Portuguese gloss. Restore the missing initial I; the group name retains its tilde over e, grave over u and plural s, and is an embedded Japanese term.
A separate Iixa pairs tera and yaxiro, a Buddhist temple and a kami shrine. The Portuguese starts Varela, & ermida and is completed by dos Camis on the next physical line.
Dos Camis completes the shrine definition. It is an indented continuation, not a headword; Camis is the Japanese divine term pluralized inside the Portuguese explanation.
Iixacu here means pouring or drawing for oneself, mizzucara cumu. The Portuguese begins taking or pouring wine, and the visible lan- continues as çar below.

runs.text: çar no copo vinho por ſi.

lines.note: Çar completes lançar; the full gloss is pouring wine into the cup for oneself. Restore the visible continuation indentation and keep the cedilla and final por ſi.
This separate Iixacu is a lodestone, not self-pouring. Restore the upright I in the repeated example headword; the following curo- begins curogane, iron, continued on the next row.

runs.text: A pedra de ceuar atrae o ferro.

lines.note: Ganeuo completes curoganeuo, and sǔ states attraction or drawing in. The Portuguese confirms that a lodestone attracts iron; retain the printed short s and caron-marked u, and restore continuation indentation.
Iixei means two particular stars, explicitly futatçuno foxi. The definition names them on the following rows; the comma here does not finish the entry.

The first star is Qengiǔ; the final vowel is a damaged u under a visible caron, not b. The other name begins with upright Xo at the right edge without a printed hyphen, and continues below. Both names are embedded in the Portuguese explanation.

Cugio completes the printed name Xocugio from the preceding row. The far-right Iixei. is a separate catchword, not part of this sentence; it is preserved under cw-l001 in a catchword zone. The original crop shows both elements and the bottom rule.
